title: WIP: BER: check for invalid length octet = 0xFF

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • e47aa686 - WIP: BER: check for invalid length octet = 0xFF
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/6620/diffs?diff_id=368057355&start_sha=39d09b75db11efcb5243b65cbe977820b5cbfcd0)
So should we throw an exception in this case (like ReportedBoundsError in line 1294)?
While in the area, should we add a check if len > 4 (which will lead to a tmp_length overflow)? We might delay it for another time

You can use %(ACTX)s->pinfo in the conformance field to have access to the pinfo structure:
```
tmp_offset = get_ber_length(%(ACTX)s->pinfo, tree, tvb, tmp_offset, &tmp_length, &tmp_ind);
```
Same applies to other conformance files.

Working to recreate this.  
Related to `GOOSE` in Ask questions and Gitlab issues/Merge Requests?  
  
[Information technology – ASN.1 encoding rules:
Specification of Basic Encoding Rules (BER),
Canonical Encoding Rules (CER) and
Distinguished Encoding Rules (DER) 
](https://www.itu.int/ITU-T/studygroups/com17/languages/X.690-0207.pdf)
